A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same adversarial-attack research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, allowing retained, renamed, relocated, added, and removed material to be matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original SDEdit and LoRA experiments on CelebA-HQ and WikiArt, alongside transferability, denoising, target-selection, memory, and prompt experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark and supplementary results and adds empirical comparisons of adversarial errors, reverse biases, and sampling biases.

M1.justification: ITA/ITA+ correspond to ACE/ACE+ in the alternating fine-tuning and clipped image-update algorithm, Mist-derived target, and optional encoder loss. However, v2 Equation 9 minimizes noise-prediction distance, whereas v3 Equation 12 maximizes score-prediction distance, despite target-attraction prose and Algorithm 1 retaining gradient descent. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents an actual objective change or an inconsistent reformulation.

E1.justification: CelebA-HQ, WikiArt, SDEdit, LoRA, and cross-model evaluation remain. V3 removes the community-supplied illustration case tested under entirely unknown LoRA conditions in v2 Appendix B.3/Figure 6. Its new held-out, same-identity mechanism tests do not establish a new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: PhotoGuard+ joins the main effectiveness comparison in v3 Table 1 and the output-image grids; v2 evaluated it only in the memory comparison. Anti-DB-T disappears from the target-image comparison retained as v3 Figure 9. Anti-DB becoming ASPL is a rename, not a new comparator.

E3.justification: V3 introduces clean-versus-adversarial fine-tuning controls and held-out, same-identity sampling simulations for mechanism validation. Reported existing settings also change: WikiArt's training prompt changes, CLIP-IQA prompts lose 'sks', and Section 5.1 specifies five fine-tuning iterations instead of v2's four. V3 inconsistently states five steps per iteration in Section 4.3 versus ten in Section 5.1. These are documented protocol revisions, without establishing that retained results were recomputed.

E4.justification: V3 Sections 3–4 add substantial analyses testing whether fine-tuning reverses adversarial errors and whether shared error patterns transfer to sampling biases. These replace v2 Appendix B.2's simpler U-Net-error comparison. The Anti-DB-T target comparison and community case are removed, while target-density, denoising, prompt, and cross-model analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix B.2 explicitly estimates mean U-Net error using 100 random timestep/noise samples per image. That sampling-count disclosure disappears with the replaced analysis; v3 Appendix A.5 specifies averaging cosine similarities over all image pairs instead. Neither version reports independent-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds mechanism findings, including reverse-bias correlations of -0.205 and -0.370 and sampling-bias cosine similarities of -0.304395 for ACE, -0.009372 for AntiDB, and -0.004139 for AdvDM. It also adds PhotoGuard+ results, including LoRA CLIP-IQA scores of 22.91 and 32.62. Corresponding pre-existing benchmark, transfer, memory, and denoising numbers remain unchanged; these do not demonstrate a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: V2's Gaussian-target/KL-divergence derivation is replaced by a score-function framework. V3 introduces inherent/adversarial error decompositions, elementwise fine-tuning discount assumptions, reverse-bias estimators, and an approximate derivation connecting shared sampling biases to accumulated sampling error. These are substantive new mathematical assumptions and arguments, beyond notation changes.

C1.justification: V2 foregrounds an improved targeted objective and sub-6-GB implementation as its two contributions. V3 foregrounds explaining adversarial fine-tuning dynamics and controlling sampling-error patterns through ACE. Memory efficiency remains in the appendix but ceases to be a headline contribution; the conclusion adds the prospect of improving attacks through target optimization.

C2.justification: V3 develops a learned reverse-bias and shared-pattern explanation substantially beyond v2's U-Net-error discussion. It acknowledges systematic error in the clean-model bias estimate and uses simulated sampling because the actual sampling score is inaccessible. Section 5.2 also reframes the human/model mismatch discussion around quantitative metrics understating visible degradation and leaves target optimization to future work.

D1.justification: V3 adds latent-heatmap normalization and cosine-computation details, specifies PhotoGuard's SD1.5 surrogate, documents PhotoGuard+'s all-pixel inpainting mask and A100 hardware, and identifies baseline notebooks more precisely. The xFormers/checkpointing implementation, 5.77-GB memory result, and 1739-second runtime are retained after relocation.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from targeted-objective design and practical memory efficiency to explaining why adversarial examples disrupt LDM fine-tuning, explicitly contrasting classification-model adversarial training. V3 adds relevant score-based, adversarial-training, prompt-poisoning, and score-distillation references while removing much of the targeted-transfer discussion and the DUAW comparison.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, methodological narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around attack dynamics. ITA/ITA+ become ACE/ACE+, the title and author presentation change, memory and denoising sections move into the appendix, and the appendices are reorganized. This substantially changes the document's narrative structure.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main layout, adds dynamics diagrams and bias heatmaps, expands comparison grids with PhotoGuard+, and extensively relocates and reformats retained displays. The target comparison loses its Anti-DB-T column. Figure 12 also appears to interchange ACE/ACE+ labels on the reused SDEdit outputs relative to v2 Figure 8.

improvement.justification: The new controlled bias comparisons address v2's largely qualitative mechanism explanation, and PhotoGuard+ broadens benchmarking. However, v3's central objective conflicts with Algorithm 1, fine-tuning counts conflict, and revised prompts accompany unchanged scores without explaining their relationship. These ambiguities affect reproducibility and interpretation of the expanded claims. The substantive additions and reporting problems leave the net quality effect uncertain.
